description: 45 drone company logos explained by a brand designer, from DJI, Skydio, and Parrot to Zipline, Wing, Anduril, and Joby Aviation.
intro:
Drone logos have to work in the sky, on a remote controller, on an app icon, and on the side of a delivery box, so the best ones are simple, fast-looking, and easy to read from far away.

What makes a good drone logo?

Motion: italic letters, swooshes, and arrows, like DJI, DroneUp, and Wing, tell you the product flies before you read the name.

A symbol from flight: wings, rotors seen from above, and flight paths give drone brands an ownable mark, from Manna's four-lobed flower to Joby's looping line.

Durability: drone logos are printed on small aircraft, controllers, and boxes, so bold shapes and one or two colors work best.

Below are 45 drone company logos in five groups, from consumer camera drones to delivery, public safety, defense, and air taxis. Each one has a slide with my handwritten notes, followed by a short explanation. For more machines that move on their own, see my review of robotics logos.

logoResearch.name: DJI
logoResearch.verifiedFact: DJI is a Shenzhen-based company and the world's largest maker of consumer camera drones.
observations: The heavy, italic lowercase letters lean forward like a drone in flight.
DJI blue and a custom, connected letterform make three letters feel like a symbol.

logoResearch.name: Autel Robotics
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Autel Robotics is a Shenzhen drone maker known for its EVO camera drones.
observations: A bold red wordmark with a squared A looks technical and confident.
ROBOTICS in small spaced grey caps works as a descriptor.

logoResearch.name: Parrot
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Parrot is a French drone company known for its ANAFI drones.
observations: A classic serif wordmark is a rare, elegant choice in a technical category.
The name is a bird, a natural fit for a company that makes flying machines.

logoResearch.name: Skydio
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Skydio is a US maker of autonomous drones for public safety, inspection, and defense.
observations: The symbol is a bold black shape cut by a curved line, like a wing or a flight path.
Using the mark alone, Skydio keeps the identity compact for products and apps.

logoResearch.name: Yuneec
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Yuneec is a drone maker known for its Typhoon and H520 series.
observations: Custom, angular capitals with cut strokes give the name a technical, futuristic look.
The heavy black letters keep the unusual shapes legible.

logoResearch.name: Hubsan
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Hubsan is a Shenzhen maker of consumer and hobby drones.
observations: A large, stylized H anchors a smaller wordmark.
Small caps for the rest of the name make the logo feel like a badge.

logoResearch.name: Holy Stone
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Holy Stone is a consumer and beginner drone brand.
observations: An H in a circle with motion lines suggests spinning propellers.
Italic, stacked type in grey adds a sense of speed.

logoResearch.name: Potensic
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Potensic is a consumer drone brand known for the Atom series.
observations: A heavy italic wordmark with a custom P leans forward with energy.
The black, compact name is easy to print on small drones and boxes.

logoResearch.name: HoverAir
logoResearch.verifiedFact: HoverAir makes small self-flying camera drones from Zero Zero Robotics.
observations: The name is split into bold HOVER and light Air.
Small, wide capitals keep it minimal, like a consumer electronics brand.

logoResearch.name: Zipline
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Zipline is a US company that delivers medical supplies and packages by drone.
observations: Two stacked chevrons form a Z and suggest fast movement.
A bold, friendly sans wordmark makes delivery feel simple.

logoResearch.name: Wing
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Wing is Alphabet's drone delivery company.
observations: An arrow corner pointing up and right sits next to the name, like a drone taking off.
A deep purple wordmark sets it apart from the blue of most tech brands.

logoResearch.name: Manna
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Manna is an Irish drone delivery company based in Dublin.
observations: The four-lobed symbol looks like a flower or a quadcopter seen from above.
A clean, black wordmark keeps the brand friendly and simple.

logoResearch.name: Flytrex
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Flytrex is a drone delivery company focused on suburban food delivery.
observations: Thin, wide capitals with open strokes give the name a futuristic look.
The E is drawn with three lines, a custom detail that makes it memorable.

logoResearch.name: Draganfly
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Draganfly is a Canadian drone company and one of the oldest commercial drone makers.
observations: Rounded, custom letters connect the long name into one shape.
The name plays on dragonfly, a natural flying machine.

logoResearch.name: DroneUp
logoResearch.verifiedFact: DroneUp is a US drone delivery and services company.
observations: An orange swoosh in front of the name suggests a fast flight path.
A heavy wordmark with a capital U spells out the two words.

logoResearch.name: Elroy Air
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Elroy Air builds the Chaparral, an autonomous cargo aircraft.
observations: A single looping line draws a wing, an orbit, or an aircraft banking.
Black, line-only drawing keeps the mark light and fast.

logoResearch.name: Wingcopter
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Wingcopter is a German maker of tilt-rotor delivery drones.
observations: Thin, spaced capitals make the long name calm and precise.
A small triangle mark at the end looks like an aircraft seen from above.

logoResearch.name: Arrive AI
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Arrive AI makes smart mailboxes that receive drone and robot deliveries.
observations: A green dot under the i shows a delivery landing on its spot.
A soft lowercase wordmark with a green ai keeps it friendly.

logoResearch.name: Brinc
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Brinc is a US maker of drones for police and first responders.
observations: A geometric lowercase wordmark with no symbol looks calm and modern.
The light, rounded letters avoid the aggressive look of many public safety brands.

logoResearch.name: Flock Safety
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Flock Safety is a public safety technology company whose products include drones for first responders.
observations: A small figure-like mark sits next to a heavy wordmark.
Bold black type makes the brand feel solid and serious.

logoResearch.name: Percepto
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Percepto makes autonomous drone-in-a-box systems for industrial sites.
observations: A faceted, geometric mark looks like a crystal or a scanning sensor.
Wide, rounded capitals keep the long name readable.

logoResearch.name: Flyability
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Flyability is a Swiss maker of collision-tolerant drones for indoor inspection.
observations: The mark looks like a propeller blade inside a protective curve, like its caged drones.
Thin, spaced capitals feel technical and precise.

logoResearch.name: Freefly Systems
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Freefly Systems makes camera drones and gimbals for film and industry.
observations: Wide, outlined capitals give the name a sporty, cinematic look.
With no symbol, the custom wordmark carries the brand.

logoResearch.name: Inspired Flight
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Inspired Flight is a US maker of heavy-lift commercial drones.
observations: The IFT monogram is drawn with thick, broken lines like an engineering diagram.
Black only, the mark looks industrial and strong.

logoResearch.name: Red Cat
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Red Cat is a US drone technology company that owns Teal Drones.
observations: A red cat face in the middle of the name is a literal, memorable symbol.
Squared, stencil-like letters give it a military feel.

logoResearch.name: Easy Aerial
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Easy Aerial makes tethered and autonomous drone systems.
observations: The E letters are drawn with three separate lines.
Thin, wide capitals with EZ for easy make the name playful.

logoResearch.name: EagleNXT
logoResearch.verifiedFact: EagleNXT, formerly AgEagle Aerial Systems, makes the eBee drones and agriculture sensors.
observations: A purple eagle with spread wings sits above the name.
Wide, spaced capitals with NXT for next mark the 2025 rebrand.

logoResearch.name: Anduril
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Anduril is a US defense technology company that makes autonomous systems and drones.
observations: The A mark is an outlined, abstract shape, like a sword tip or an aircraft.
Heavy capitals named after a sword from The Lord of the Rings feel strong and mythic.

logoResearch.name: Shield AI
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Shield AI is a US defense company that builds AI pilots and the V-BAT drone.
observations: A shield symbol made of small pieces suggests protection built from data.
The wordmark only says Shield, letting the symbol imply the AI.

logoResearch.name: AeroVironment
logoResearch.verifiedFact: AeroVironment (AV) is a US maker of military drones such as Switchblade and Puma.
observations: The AV letters are drawn with outlines and a blue swoosh like a flight path.
Shortening the long name to two letters makes it easy to put on aircraft.

logoResearch.name: Neros
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Neros is a US startup that builds low-cost FPV drones for defense.
observations: An N in a shield-like frame sits next to spaced capitals.
Black and simple, it looks like a defense badge.

logoResearch.name: Helsing
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Helsing is a German defense AI company that also builds strike drones.
observations: The mark is an H made from two bars with a small line in the middle.
Pure black and very simple, it works as a stamp on any product.

logoResearch.name: Quantum Systems
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Quantum Systems is a German maker of eVTOL surveillance drones.
observations: Custom, wide capitals with a cut U look technical and futuristic.
The tagline The Future is Unmanned sits next to the name.

logoResearch.name: Tekever
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Tekever is a Portuguese maker of surveillance drones such as the AR3 and AR5.
observations: The K is drawn as an arrow, adding motion to the letters.
Wide, angular capitals look precise and engineered.

logoResearch.name: Baykar
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Baykar is a Turkish defense company and the maker of the Bayraktar TB2 drone.
observations: A small B mark sits next to wide, bold capitals.
Black and blocky, it feels industrial and serious.

logoResearch.name: Performance Drone Works
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Performance Drone Works (PDW) is a US maker of FPV and tactical drones for the military.
observations: A red circle with a white triangle sits next to heavy PDW letters.
The triangle reads as an arrow or a drone pointing up.

logoResearch.name: Auterion
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Auterion builds an operating system for drones based on open-source PX4.
observations: A bold wordmark with a custom A carries the brand with no symbol.
The heavy black type looks solid, like the software foundation it sells.

logoResearch.name: DroneDeploy
logoResearch.verifiedFact: DroneDeploy is a drone and reality-capture software platform, now part of Procore.
observations: A circle with a downward triangle looks like a map pin or a camera looking down.
FROM PROCORE under the name shows the new parent company.

logoResearch.name: Pix4D
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Pix4D is a Swiss company that makes photogrammetry and mapping software.
observations: A green, folded mark looks like a 3D surface or a mountain mapped from above.
Spaced capitals in dark blue sit under the symbol.

logoResearch.name: Joby Aviation
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Joby Aviation is a US company developing electric air taxis.
observations: The looping mark is a single line that draws a flight path or an infinity loop.
A friendly, rounded wordmark makes air travel feel approachable.

logoResearch.name: Archer Aviation
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Archer Aviation is a US company developing the Midnight electric air taxi.
observations: The mark is a set of curved lines like a bow, a nod to the name.
Wide, spaced capitals give the brand a premium, aerospace look.

logoResearch.name: EHang
logoResearch.verifiedFact: EHang is a Chinese company that makes autonomous passenger aircraft such as the EH216.
observations: Custom, rounded capitals in English and Chinese sit side by side.
The bilingual logo shows a company built for global markets.

logoResearch.name: Wisk
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Wisk is a Boeing-owned company developing self-flying air taxis.
observations: A yellow, handwritten script ends in a long slash like a takeoff.
The script feels personal and light, unusual for aerospace.

logoResearch.name: Beta Technologies
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Beta Technologies is a US company building electric aircraft.
observations: A lightning bolt is cut into the B, signaling electric power.
Heavy, slanted capitals look fast and bold.

logoResearch.name: Volocopter
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Volocopter is a German developer of electric air taxis.
observations: A V mark made of curved lines looks like rotors seen from above.
Spaced capitals in black keep the long name clean.

listIntro: The boards below show all 45 drone logos in one consistent format, grouped into consumer drones, delivery, enterprise and public safety, defense, and drone software and air taxis.
Each logo is reviewed for its design decisions, not for the quality of the aircraft.
sectionIntroductions: Consumer drone brands sell to hobbyists and creators, so their logos lean on bold, fast-looking wordmarks.
Delivery drone companies have to feel friendly over people's homes, so their logos are simple, light, and often playful.
Enterprise and public safety brands sell to police, utilities, and industry, and their logos favor clean, technical capitals.
Defense drone makers use stark, black, badge-like logos that feel serious and engineered.
Drone software and air taxi companies sell the future of flight, with logos that mix flight paths, rotors, and premium aerospace type.
sectionBridge: This is a visual comparison of drone company logos, not a ranking of drones.
Look at how each logo suggests flight and how it would look on the aircraft itself.
entryFallbacks: The identity relies on a few clear decisions to stay recognizable.
Notice how the logo would look printed on a small aircraft or a controller.

findings.heading: Motion is the category's shortcut
findings.text: Italic letters, swooshes, and arrows in DJI, DroneUp, Wing, and Potensic tell you the product flies.

findings.heading: Flight inspires the best symbols
findings.text: Manna's four-lobed flower, Volocopter's rotor V, and Joby's looping line come straight from how drones and air taxis fly.

findings.heading: Defense brands go black and badge-like
findings.text: Anduril, Helsing, Neros, and Baykar use stark black marks that look like military insignia.

findings.heading: Delivery brands stay friendly
findings.text: Zipline, Wing, Manna, and Arrive AI use soft shapes and friendly type because their drones fly over people's homes.

logoRosterConfig.checklistHeading: A practical checklist for a new drone logo
checklistItems: Does the logo suggest flight or motion without a cliche propeller icon?
Is it readable from far away and when printed small on the aircraft?
Does it work in one color for stickers, controllers, and packaging?
Does it fit your audience: consumers, cities, industry, or defense?
Will the symbol still work as an app icon?

faq.question: What makes a good drone company logo?
faq.answer: A good drone logo suggests flight or motion, stays readable from far away and when printed small on the aircraft, and works in one color. The strongest examples, like DJI, Zipline, and Wing, pair a bold wordmark with a simple shape that hints at speed or a flight path.

faq.question: What does the DJI logo mean?
faq.answer: The DJI logo is a custom, heavy italic wordmark of the company's initials, from Da-Jiang Innovations. The forward lean and connected letters give the three letters the speed and compactness of a symbol.

faq.question: Which drone companies have the best logos?
faq.answer: Some of the most distinctive drone logos belong to DJI, Zipline, Wing, Manna, and Joby Aviation, which use motion and flight-inspired symbols, and to defense brands like Anduril and Helsing, which use stark, badge-like marks.
